newsitem.title: USA: Oncor gets breast cancer detection patent.
newsitem.headline: Oncor gets breast cancer detection patent.

text.p: Oncor Inc said Thursday it had received a U.S. patent covering methods for the early detection of breast cancer.
The patent -- No. 5,571,678 -- is for technology that measures the amount of an isoform of ferritin (p43) bound to lymphocytes.
Oncor said data published by Chaya Moroz of Tel Aviv University's Sackler School of Medicine, and others, has demonstrated that the p43 protein is elevated at an early stage in breast cancer.

"This patent paves the way for Oncor to develop a blood test for early (stage IIH) breast cancer, as well as in situ (localized) cancer, which may provide the opportunity to detect and treat breast cancer at an early stage," said Jeffrey Ross, Oncor's medical director.
Oncor holds an exclusive worldwide license for the patent.
